facts.text: A manufacturer of heavy off-road machines for construction, mining, quarrying and similar work already sells an object-proximity system that warns the operator.
facts.quote: already sells a system that warns the operator when the machine gets too close to an object.

facts.text: The heavy off-road machine manufacturer is developing a system that automatically applies the brakes if the operator does not react.
facts.quote: developing a system that also applies the brakes automatically if the operator does not react.

facts.text: Prototype hardware and software for the new heavy off-road machine system will arrive in mid-2027, after which validation must finish in less than four months.
facts.quote: Prototype hardware and software will arrive in mid-2027 and validation must then finish in less than four months

facts.text: Past physical testing and tuning took three to four years for each machine model.
facts.quote: in the past it took three to four years of physical testing and tuning for each machine model.

facts.text: The new automatic-braking system must work across more than 100 types of job site and more than 10 operating scenarios per machine.
facts.quote: The new system must work across more than 100 types of job site, more than 10 operating scenarios per machine

facts.text: The new automatic-braking system must work in rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness and glare.
facts.quote: many weather and light conditions (rain, snow, fog, dust, dusk, darkness, glare)

facts.text: The new automatic-braking system must work across many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.
facts.quote: many machine models with different sizes and sensor positions.

facts.text: Sensor types for the new system are not confirmed, so the research had to cover camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other options.
facts.quote: The sensor types are not confirmed, so camera, radar, lidar, ultrasonic and other options all had to be covered.

facts.text: The research sought methods for measuring an existing object detection and warning system without driving the machine.
facts.quote: learn how an existing object detection and warning system can be measured without driving the machine

facts.text: The research sought ways to compare a new system fairly against an existing object detection and warning system.
facts.quote: how a new system can be compared against it fairly.

facts.text: The research was to investigate the prerequisites and evidential scope of off-field testing methods: recorded sensor-data replay, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, signal injection into real sensors and vehicle-in-the-loop.
facts.quote: including replay of recorded sensor data, software-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, injecting signals into real sensors and vehicle-in-the-loop? What does each need, and what does each prove?

facts.text: The research was to compare reference sensors, manual labeling, automatic labeling and surveyed test targets as ways of establishing ground truth for recorded field data.
facts.quote: How is the true situation ("ground truth") established for recorded field data? Reference sensors, manual labeling, automatic labeling and surveyed test targets were to be compared.

facts.text: The research was to investigate how to build a performance baseline, including detection rate by distance and object type, false alarms per hour, warning timing and the amount of data needed.
facts.quote: How is a performance baseline built? Which measures are used (detection rate by distance and object type, false alarms per hour, warning timing), and how much data is needed?

facts.text: The research was to investigate what can and cannot be compared directly between old and new systems when sensors, sensor positions or software differ.
facts.quote: How can a new system be compared with an old one when the sensors, the sensor positions or the software are different? What can be compared directly, and what cannot?

facts.text: Once a system can brake, recorded data no longer match what happens next; the research sought ways to handle this difference between replay testing and interactive closed-loop testing.
facts.quote: Once a system can brake, recorded data no longer match what happens next. How do teams handle this difference between replay testing and interactive (closed-loop) testing?

facts.text: The research was to investigate how to test a new system before its final hardware exists.
facts.quote: How do teams test a new system before its final hardware exists?

facts.text: The research was to investigate which machine data must be recorded for later replay and the common recording mistakes.
facts.quote: What must be recorded on the machine to make later replay possible, and what are the common mistakes?

facts.text: The research was required to remain neutral across vendors, products and technologies and cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.
facts.quote: The research was to stay neutral across vendors, products and technologies and to cover commercial, open-source, academic and in-house options.

facts.text: Each important research claim was required to carry an evidence-type label: independent study, standard or third-party test; vendor's own claim; or expert opinion.
facts.quote: Each important claim was to be labeled by its type of evidence (independent study, standard or third-party test; the vendor's own claim; or expert opinion)

facts.text: Each research source was required to be dated, with a preference for sources from 2023 or later for tools and products.
facts.quote: each source was to be dated, with a preference for sources from 2023 or later for tools and products.

facts.text: The research was required to report failures, limits and evidence against each approach, rather than only successes.
facts.quote: Failures, limits and evidence against each approach were to be reported, not only successes.

facts.text: Research findings proven only for on-road vehicles were required to be flagged as on-road-only evidence.
facts.quote: Anything proven only for on-road vehicles had to be flagged as such

facts.text: When the research could find no evidence, the answer was required to be “not found” rather than a guessed number, price or timeline.
facts.quote: where nothing could be found the answer was to be "not found" rather than a guessed number, price or timeline.
